summary: Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Lobsang Gyatso. He also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tenga Rinpoche studied at Benchen Monastery. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery around 1967 to 1984, founded Benchen Monastery in 1976, and taught Karl Brunnhölzl.

Kitabatake studied Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University (ca. 1951–1955). He served at Ryukoku as assistant, lecturer, associate professor (1955), professor (1970), department director (1989–1993), and president (1995–1999), and was president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sogen Omori, whom he eventually succeeded. He also founded Chozen-ji.

Tenzin Dorjee works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Sonam Rinchen, Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, and Geshe Dawa, and served as translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery.

Tenzin Namdak studied under Shes rab bstan 'dzin rgyal mtshan, Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and at Menri Monastery, earning a lha rams pa degree. He worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery in 1986.

Specializing in Tibetology, Tenzin Namgha earned a Ph.D. from Christ University (2010–2016). His career includes positions at the Dalai Lama Institute for Higher Education (2019–2021) and Central Tibetan Administration (2021), and an external research affiliation at York University (2026).

Tenzin Norbu is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who taught Laura Harrington. He held a post at Columbia University and served as an Assistant Professor and department head at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Tenzin Tsenyi works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Warsaw, where she also served as an assistant-academic teacher from 2024 to 2025.

Active in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he earned a Geshe degree at Menri Monastery. He held posts as director at the Dialectic School of Menri, president at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and founded Ligmincha Institute.
Teodor Iordănescu was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bucharest (ca. 1892–1897) and the University of Halle (1901–1903) under Richard Pischel, Richard Schmidt, and Eugen Hultzsch.

Ellingson studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he was a music professor at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.
Terence Dukes was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He founded Kongoryuji Temple in 1978 and taught there.

Bartholomew studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, earning an M.A. Active in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology, she served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum.

Terry Kleeman, a scholar of sinology and religious studies, studied at the University of British Columbia from around 1979 to 1982. He became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998.
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Ishizu studied at the University of Tokyo and worked in religious studies and philosophy. His major posts included president of Tohoku University (1963–1966) and Miyagi University of Education (1965), as well as professorships at Keio University and Komazawa University.

A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, Bartholomeusz studied at Florida State University and the University of Virginia, among others. She held teaching posts at Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis, and was Professor of Religion at Florida State.
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in history and archaeology. She studied at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato studied Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University between 1925 and 1931. He served as a professor at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University, and was named professor emeritus at Ryukoku University.
